questions.stem: An angle at the centre of a circle is $140°$. What is the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc?
questions.explanation: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference: $140° \div 2 = 70°$.

questions.stem: An angle in a semicircle (angle subtended by a diameter) is always:
questions.explanation: The angle in a semicircle is always $90°$. This follows from the fact that the diameter subtends an angle of $180°$ at the centre, so the angle at the circumference is $180° \div 2 = 90°$.

questions.stem: Two angles at the circumference are subtended by the same arc. One is $35°$. What is the other?
questions.explanation: Angles in the same segment (subtended by the same arc) are equal, so the other angle is also $35°$.

questions.stem: A cyclic quadrilateral has one angle of $82°$. What is the opposite angle?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180°$: $180° - 82° = 98°$.

questions.stem: A tangent meets a radius at the point of contact. The angle between them is:
questions.explanation: A tangent is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so the angle is $90°$.

questions.stem: An angle at the circumference is $x°$. The angle at the centre subtended by the same arc is:
questions.explanation: The angle at the centre is always twice the angle at the circumference when both are subtended by the same arc.

questions.stem: In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, angle $A = 3x$ and angle $C = 2x + 10$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles sum to $180°$: $3x + 2x + 10 = 180$, so $5x = 170$ and $x = 34$.
